title: a path crosses the inspect wire by its root, not by the asking box's disk
intention: A Path that crosses codemother's inspect wire from under a known root (the caller's cairn checkout or its CairnCommons) arrives as that root plus a relative path, and the answering judge resolves it against its own checkout of the same root. A path under neither root crosses as itself tagged with the caller's host, and is rebuilt only on that same host; on any other host it is refused loudly, never resolved as a missing file.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 on akienasus: CAIRN_BUS_HOME=akiendelllinux.local:7419, so /sorted's reason_has_referent (skills/sorted/door.py:64) asks the Dell's codemother over inspect, the Path crosses as its plain string (inspect_wire.py:31 {'__wire__':'path','v':str(value)}), and /home/akien/cairn/... does not exist on the Dell, so every 'none, because <repo path>' reason is refused as having no referent. Ticket-id referents still resolve. Every judge taking a Path answers from the wrong disk whenever caller and bus host differ; a Windows caller (C:\automation\local\cairn) sends backslashes no Linux judge can open.
traces_to: Law 3 (a judge's answer is a measurement of the caller's world, so it must read the same file the caller named); Law 7 (a path the wire cannot place is refused by name, never answered False); RULE 1 (the fix lives in the one module holding both directions of the wire, so no judge or door patches it alone).
how: In cairn/tools/inspect_wire/inspect_wire.py, the path kind changes shape: wire_encode resolves a Path and, when it lies under one of the known roots, sends {'__wire__':'path','root':'cairn'|'CairnCommons','rel':<posix relpath>}; wire_decode joins rel (split on both / and \) onto its own checkout of that root. The known roots are named in one function, _roots(), returning {'cairn': the checkout this module is imported from (Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]), 'CairnCommons': cairn.tools.edges.edges.commons_root()} (a tool using a tool). A Path under neither root crosses as {'__wire__':'path','root':'abs','host':socket.gethostname(),'v':<abs posix>}; wire_decode rebuilds it only when host equals its own gethostname() and otherwise raises ValueError naming the path and both hosts (same-box scratch worlds keep working; an off-root path from another box is refused at the answerer). A decoded root the answerer does not know raises at decode. A relative Path is resolved against cwd before the test. The old {'v': str} form is gone (no compatibility lane: both directions ship in one module). The proof drives the codec with caller and answerer roots set to two different scratch trees (by monkeypatching _roots per side), and asks reason_has_referent through ask() in a launched codemother whose roots differ from the caller's.

outcomes.claim: a Path under the caller's cairn root, encoded with caller roots A and decoded with answerer roots B, rebuilds as the same relative path under B's cairn root; likewise for CairnCommons

the /sorted 'none, because <repo path>' reason naming a file that exists under the answerer's checkout but at a different absolute path than the caller's is judged True through ask() (a launched codemother whose roots differ from the caller's)

an off-root absolute Path encoded on host A and decoded on host B raises ValueError naming the path and both hosts, and an encoded path naming an unknown root raises at wire_decode; neither is ever answered False
a path kind whose rel carries backslashes (a Windows caller) decodes on Linux to the same file as its forward-slash spelling
an off-root absolute Path (a scratch world under /tmp) encoded and decoded on the same host rebuilds equal, so codemother's test_codemother_answers_inspect_over_the_bus.py tooth 3 stands unchanged
